text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Central planning office CPB sees price incentives as possible means to curb the growth of mobility in the Netherlands. (p1)
- Northwest Airlines seeks to put pressure on its partner KLM to settle their dispute. (p1)
- Trading floor of the Amsterdam Options Exchange will move to the building of the Amsterdam Stock Exchange next year. (p1)
- Retailer Ahold sees competition growing in Thailand. (p3)
- Private investors are the motor behind the current strong rise of the Amsterdam Stock Exchange. (p13)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Debate about Schiphol's growth ends in sharp conflict between employers' association and the environmentalists. (p1)
- Shareholders' lobby group VEB wants tougher policy against insider trading. (p2)
- Transport group Nedlloyd's chief puts up pressure on Danish shipowner Maersk. (p31)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Pensionfunds, which own shopping malls, start offensive against mail order and new media. (p33)
- Office furniture supplier Samas optimistic about prospects of lifting its results. (p35)
TROUW
- Shell Nederland boosts its 1996 net by 39 pct to Dfl 2.6 bn. (p7)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Internet access providers turn their back on PTT Telecom out of protest against PTT's plans for starting internet services. (p9)
- Union CNV fears for loss of 150 jobs at Nutricia's Zoetermeer unit. (p9)
